A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the reparameterization of multitrait single-step models to genetic principal components provides a useful tool to reduce the computational burden of the analysis, especially in the case of dense genomic information.
the genetic principal component model provides a framework for dimension reduction and sparse coefficient matrices in genetic evaluation that is applicable to a variety of applications.

the genetic principal component models are an alternative to the multivariate linear model for multitrait genetic evaluations, with reduced computational requirements and a direct connection to dimension reduction.
The main takeaway from our work is that

a principal component reparameterization of a mixed model for genetic evaluation is a viable alternative to the standard model, which is based on a Cholesky decomposition of the inverse of a relationship matrix.
genetic principal components can be used to reduce the number of parameters to estimate and to improve computational performance of the single-step approach.
genetic principal component models are a viable alternative to the classical multivariate linear mixed models.
